title: Conjecture 2 (Ossona de Mendez, Oum, and Wood)
context_text: Ossona de Mendez, Oum, and Wood conjectured that the defective chromatic number of the class of $H$-minor-free graphs equals $\mathrm{td}(H)-1$ for every graph $H$. The lower bound $\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{M}_H) \geq \mathrm{td}(H)-1$ was already established; the upper bound was known only in special cases such as $H = K_t$ and complete bipartite graphs.
attributed_to: Ossona de Mendez, Oum, and Wood
paper_contribution: Provides the first evidence for the upper bound direction by proving that $\chi^*(\mathcal{M}_H)$ — and hence $\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{M}_H)$ — is bounded above by a function of $\mathrm{td}(H)$ (specifically $\chi^*(\mathcal{M}_H) \leq 2^{\mathrm{td}(H)+1} - 4$), which was previously unknown.

title: Conjecture 4
context_text: Graphs are simple and finite. A graph is $k$-colourable with clustering $c$ if its vertices can be coloured with $k$ colours so that every monochromatic component (connected component of the subgraph induced by one colour class) has at most $c$ vertices; the clustered chromatic number $\chi_\star(\mathcal{G})$ of a class $\mathcal{G}$ is the minimum $k$ such that, for some integer $c$, every graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is $k$-colourable with clustering $c$. $\mathcal{M}_H$ is the class of $H$-minor-free graphs. For a rooted tree $T$, its depth is the maximum number of vertices on a root-to-leaf path and its closure is obtained by adding an edge between every ancestor and descendant; the connected tree-depth $\mathrm{ctd}(H)$ is the minimum depth of a rooted tree whose closure contains $H$ as a subgraph. The usual tree-depth $\mathrm{td}(H)$ is the maximum of $\mathrm{ctd}$ over the components of $H$; $\mathrm{ctd}(H)=\mathrm{td}(H)$ unless $H$ has two components of tree-depth $\mathrm{td}(H)$, in which case $\mathrm{ctd}(H)=\mathrm{td}(H)+1$. The authors prove $\mathrm{ctd}(H)-1\le\chi_\star(\mathcal{M}_H)\le 2^{\mathrm{ctd}(H)+1}-4$ for every graph $H$, and construct for each $k\ge2$ a graph $H_k$ with $\mathrm{ctd}(H_k)=\mathrm{td}(H_k)=k$ and $\chi_\star(\mathcal{M}_{H_k})\ge 2k-2$. This contrasts with defective colouring (each colour class inducing bounded maximum degree), for which Ossona de Mendez, Oum and Wood conjectured that the defective chromatic number of $\mathcal{M}_H$ equals $\mathrm{ctd}(H)-1$. The authors conjecture that the lower bound $2k-2$ is tight, and prove the conjecture when $\mathrm{ctd}(H)=3$ (four colours suffice, which is best possible). They also propose a more general conjecture for the clustered chromatic number of an arbitrary minor-closed class, which generalises this one.
